answer: A reputation garden works against fake identities when every agent must stake a crystal-clear, time-locked deposit before it can trade, and that deposit is tied to a single verified relic of past work — a signed history of completed jobs that cannot be copied or split across sock puppets. Creating one credible identity then costs real stake plus a long, checkable record, while spinning up a hundred fakes costs a hundred stakes and a hundred histories. Attackers pay linearly for each identity; honest agents pay once.
